standard.title: Choreograph to communicate ideas
standard.description: use the elements of dance to choreograph dance that communicates ideas, perspectives and/or meaning
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can use elements of dance to choreograph dance sequences (Y1-2). They have produced sequences with beginning, middle and end, made deliberate element choices, and used feedback to refine their work.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students use the elements of dance to choreograph dance that communicates ideas, perspectives and/or meaning.

nodes.label: Choreographic intent
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify and articulate a clear choreographic intent — the idea, perspective or meaning their dance will communicate.
nodes.minimum_width: Articulating one intended meaning or idea for a dance before beginning choreography — using Viewpoints questions to frame the intent.
nodes.typical_width: Using Viewpoints questions to clarify choreographic intent: 'How will the dance begin/end?', 'What shapes will we make?', 'How can we connect these parts?'; planning structure (beginning, middle, end) around a chosen idea, perspective or connection to Country/Place.
wider: Use learning from dances that communicate First Nations Australians' connection to Country/Place to frame intent — devising a dance communicating students' own connection to and responsibility for a place in their community
Investigate how dances from different cultural celebrations communicate specific ideas — using this research to frame and enrich their own choreographic intent
nodes.hinge_reason: Without a clear intent, choreographic choices become arbitrary — students select movements for visual interest rather than communicative purpose. Intent is what transforms movement arrangement into dance that communicates meaning.

response_modes.reason: Articulating intent requires rehearsal — students often discover what they want to say through movement rather than before it. Use Viewpoints questions iteratively: before, during and after choreography. Journal or verbal planning tools help crystallise intent.

success_criteria: Student can articulate what idea, feeling or perspective their dance communicates before or during the choreographic process
Student can explain how at least one element choice serves their communicative intent

nodes.label: Generating and extending movement material
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can generate movement material using improvisation and known movements, extending and varying sequences using choreographic exploration.
nodes.minimum_width: Improvising from at least one known movement type; generating two or more extension variations (e.g. at different levels, in different directions, with different dynamics).
nodes.typical_width: Improvising using locomotor and non-locomotor movements; exploring known movements to find alternative versions; using contrast and repetition to generate new material; combining running and sliding, bending and stretching; using a variety of levels and directions.
wider: Use cultural stories as stimulus — developing movements to represent different aspects of a story (character walk, mood, setting)
Explore how the same movement changes meaning when performed at different levels, with different dynamics, or in different spatial relationships with a partner

response_modes.reason: Students need material to work with before they can structure it. Prioritise movement generation across multiple sessions and stimuli before expecting students to select, combine and arrange.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Students who generate movement material from multiple starting points — stories, cultural contexts, physical exploration, contrast/repetition — develop richer choreographic options and are less likely to default to familiar gestures.
success_criteria: Student can generate at least three movement variations from one starting movement (varying level, direction, dynamics, body part, or timing)
Student demonstrates use of both locomotor and non-locomotor movements in generated material

nodes.label: Structuring and combining into whole dance
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can select, combine and structure movement material into a dance that communicates their intended meaning — using choreographic decisions to shape the whole.
nodes.minimum_width: A structured dance with clear beginning, middle and end; at least two deliberate element choices serving the communicative intent; combined with a partner or group.
nodes.typical_width: Selecting and combining locomotor and non-locomotor movements into sequences; structuring into a dance with beginning-middle-end; combining with a partner or group to extend; using Viewpoints to evaluate and refine structural choices; following protocols where content draws on First Nations knowledge.
wider: Choreograph a dance that communicates connection to and responsibility for a specific place in their community — with element choices that reflect emotional relationship to place
Extend the dance by layering a second structural device (e.g. canon, contrast section, call-and-response) to deepen the communication of meaning
nodes.hinge_reason: Producing a complete structured dance — not just movement material — is the capability milestone of this standard. Students who cannot yet structure and combine at this level will lack the compositional experience to engage with choreographic devices (Y5-6 C strand) and more complex structural forms.

response_modes.reason: Structuring integrates intent (N1) with generated material (N2) into a communicative whole. Scaffold with explicit structure prompts and repeated partner/group sharing — hearing 'what did you think my dance was about?' calibrates intent-execution alignment.

success_criteria: Student produces a dance with a clear beginning, middle and end
Student can explain how their structural choices (how it begins, how it ends) serve the communicative intent
Student can identify at least one change they made in response to feedback
